comparator.name: History (Geschiedenis)
comparator.academicYear: 2026–27 public programme and VU 2026–27 course entries; prospective Fall 2026 bachelor pathway unresolved
comparator.sourceNotes: The current VU prospectus describes a broad first-year European/world-history and source-method sequence, second-year thematic history and research colleges with some free choice, and a third-year minor or approved placement/abroad option plus research colleges and a free-topic bachelor thesis. Its year lists explicitly defer to the VU study guide for the full curriculum and do not give the EC and compulsory/choice allocation of the whole programme. VU's public 2026–27 course entries substantiate the credits below and, for the thesis, the mandatory companion colloquium. Those entries refer to the current course year; they do not on their own determine the complete second and third year of a Fall 2026 entrant. The VU OER page directs readers to the study-guide portal, whose applicable degree plan/OER could not be retrieved by the available tools. Only individually supported components are retained; the omitted, uncertain credit-bearing components and unspecified elective/minor allocation are not invented to force 180 EC.

exception.reason: The accessible current official VU prospectus is a thematic and partial course overview; it explicitly sends readers to the study guide for the complete programme. Individual VU 2026–27 course entries establish 60 EC of named components, but not the full compulsory sequence, the amount and restrictions of second-year free choice, the third-year minor/placement alternatives, or all third-year research-college credits. The applicable formal degree plan/OER is inaccessible to the available tools. Filling the other 120 EC or treating all displayed optional courses as mandatory would invent a 180-EC pathway. The UCR History response is academically plausible, but a fair lossless comparison must await a verified complete VU curriculum.
exception.curriculumContext: The generic Dutch-language Geschiedenis bachelor is the target; VU separately identifies History and International Studies and its different thesis/colloquium codes, which are not substituted here. The public History page describes the minor and the placement/abroad option without exact EC, and research-college topics rotate. The ten supported 2026–27 course credits listed sum to 60 EC; this partial subset does not purport to be a complete year or degree. Obtain the applicable 2026–27 study-guide degree structure or adopted OER and verify the choice space before reopening.
